overview: A run of Pacific systems keeps the Coast Mountains and Cascades busy through midweek, with the strongest push arriving Wednesday night into Thursday. The Northeast and northern Rockies look colder and drier early, then pick up snow showers and a rainstorm around Thanksgiving.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: A series of Pacific systems keeps snow falling on the Coast Mountains through midweek, with snow levels climbing as the air warms. Whistler's biggest day is Tuesday, when it is due 26" of snow, and its total for the window is 79". Expect rain mixing in from Wednesday, and Cypress Mountain's totals run lower because it sits farther south.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A low offshore keeps showers going over Western Washington, with heavier mountain snow in the Olympics and Cascades early in the week. A stronger front arrives Tuesday into Wednesday and brings the most snow, with Mt. Baker's biggest day on Thursday, when 22" is due. Snow levels stay low enough for mountain snow, but expect rain at lower elevations.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: A sharp cold front brings wind and a cold, dry spell Monday into Wednesday, so snow is unlikely before Thanksgiving. A rainstorm then tracks up the East Coast from late Thanksgiving through Friday, with a wintry mix possible on the front edge. Whiteface and Blue Mountain both look to see their biggest day Friday, while Killington sees freezing rain before turning to snow.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A passing trough brings light snow showers to western Wyoming Monday, with little accumulation. Tuesday and Wednesday are drier before a more active pattern starts on Thanksgiving. Jackson Hole's biggest day is Friday, and Sun Valley's totals stay small. Forecasters describe mountain snow with no impactful weather expected.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Snow and rain move in around Thursday as a weak system crosses the region. Whitewater's biggest day falls on Thursday, and its total for the window is 15". Revelstoke sees mostly flurries early in the week before snow and rain on Wednesday and Thursday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A quick system brings light snow to the higher terrain Monday afternoon into Tuesday morning, with the best chance over the San Juans and the Gore and Mosquito ranges. Forecasters expect no major travel impacts over Thanksgiving. Steamboat's biggest day is Friday, when 12" is due, and Breckenridge sees snow showers Friday.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Mostly flurries and showers early in the week give way to a rainy stretch from Wednesday into Friday. Big White's biggest day is Thursday, and its total for the window is 10". Sun Peaks and SilverStar see only light amounts.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A fast trough brings only light snow showers to the higher terrain Monday, with little accumulation. Tuesday through Wednesday stays quiet and dry, and holiday travel looks mostly clear. Powder Mountain's biggest day is Friday, when 9" is due, but forecasters have low confidence in the weekend pattern.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center expects the Thanksgiving East Coast storm to track closer to the coast, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and high surf. Its discussion also says the next Pacific system reaches the West Coast around the weekend of Nov 28-29, with uncertainty over how deep it is.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
